title: Bind typed file inputs in a custom MSBuild task
goal: Resolve project-relative file inputs and retain item metadata when a custom build task must run safely under ordinary or experimental multithreaded MSBuild.

selectionNotes: Select the actual task host independently of application target. No SDK-10 typed-task or .NET Framework host route is advertised.
Actual SDK 10 already has TaskEnvironment and -mt infrastructure. Generic task items and environment-constructor selection are the new boundary in this comparison.
Experimental -mt requires an explicit opt-in; the ordinary host remains a verified alternative. The attribute is a thread-safety promise, not enforcement.

runtime.name: .NET
runtime.reason: Qualified task execution host and runtime closure for the RC2 task assembly; actual GA remains unqualified.

sdk.name: .NET SDK
sdk.reason: Direct SDK assembly references require the exact artifact-qualified MSBuild 18.12.0-1.26504.105 binding and construction implementation.

language.name: C#
language.reason: Pinned language mode of the compiled typed-task example; no newer language feature is a separate task-binding requirement.

packageAssets: SDK Microsoft.Build.Framework.dll and Microsoft.Build.Utilities.Core.dll, Private=false; host-owned MSBuild 18.12.0-1.26504.105 closure. No NuGet package replacements were used.
platforms: Windows x64 with the exact .NET-hosted SDK/runtime/reference assets; other hosts and OSes are not qualified by these runs.
prerequisites: Use the exact SDK global.json pin with rollForward=disable and allowPrerelease=true; inspect effective shared build/package configuration.
Use trusted project inputs, absolute task assembly paths and separate report directories per project. No optional native tools or device are needed.

PowerShell 7 for repository capture/inspection; SDK 10.0.402 with .NET 10.0.13 is additionally required to reproduce the older comparison. Build/run the net10.0 sample before the net11.0 proof, which loads the older compatibility DLL.
constraints: No down-level generic-item route, independent NuGet replacement, Visual Studio/.NET Framework MSBuild.exe or NativeAOT compatibility is claimed.
The separate net10.0 compatibility probe uses only SDK-10 APIs. Keeping a parameterless constructor does not make the net11 typed task load on an older runtime/API closure.
Typed absolute paths do not prove existence, permission, containment or symlink safety. The sample checks missing files and assumes trusted inputs.
Proof explicitly sets MSBUILDUSESERVER=0 in disposable children; it verifies actual -mt thread nodes, not server reuse or performance.
Playbook embeds offline guidance; retrieving a recipe executes no consumer code and changes no project.
optIns: Use -mt (with -m:2 in the proof) for experimental multithreaded execution; annotate only fully audited thread-safe task classes.
stabilityLimitations: RC2 execution is not actual-GA proof; PIN-963 and PIN-959 remain open.
The migration analyzer described in preview sources is planned, not shipped or required.

evidence.scope: Actual SDK10 explicit-path task: ordinary and -mt sidecar project builds, inputs/content/output metadata, unchanged task process state, missing-file failure and parameterless construction of the compatibility binary. Exact MSBuild/compiler/ref/native-host hashes checked. No older generic-item support is claimed.

Actual SDK11 typed binding and output metadata, ordinary and actual -mt same-process/different-thread rendezvous, project paths, configured/absent defaults and explicit override, full process state equality across Execute(), canonical production XML execution and missing-file failure. The same SDK10 compatibility DLL selects its injected constructor here. Exact MSBuild/compiler/ref/native-host hashes checked. Windows x64 RC2; no server reuse, performance or actual-GA claim.

humanProof.scope: Bounded managed task execution is demonstrated by real local host builds and installed offline retrieval. No native/device/Human operation is required; unrelated Human and comprehensive/actual-GA gates remain open.
